# Uposatha Sutta (Ud 5.5 (PTS Ud 51))

**ID:** Ud 5.5 (PTS Ud 51)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)

**Title (Pali):** Uposatha Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uposatha Sutta* (Ud 5.5; PTS Ud 51–53) is the fifth discourse of the *Soṇavagga* (or *Soṇatherassavagga*), the fifth chapter of the *Udāna* [Lueritthikul 2015]. In the discourse's opening narrative, the Buddha refuses to recite the Pātimokkha because the assembled Saṅgha is impure; Venerable Mahā Moggallāna discerns the unvirtuous individual and physically expels the sham monk from the assembly [Lueritthikul 2015]. Following this disciplinary action, the Buddha delivers an elaborate discourse drawing an eightfold comparison between the marvelous qualities of the great ocean and the virtues of the Dhamma-Vinaya [Lueritthikul 2015].

 In comparative Vinaya literature, the narrative aligns with the *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu* preserved in the Gilgit manuscript of the *Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya* [Lueritthikul 2015]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns the text with various Chinese sūtras, notably the *Fǎhǎi jīng* (T 34), *Zhānpó bǐqiū jīng* (T 64), and sections of the *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125), Sanskrit fragments of the *Pravāraṇāvastu* and *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Śamathadeva's Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094) [DharmaNexus]. The sutta is also referenced across later canonical and paracanonical works, including the *Milindapañha*, *Kathāvatthu*, *Parivāra*, *Nettippakaraṇa*, and *Peṭakopadesa*.
